$comment: First-load JS per route, gzipped, in kilobytes. Checked by scripts/check-bundle-budget.ts.
Seeded from a real build with ~3% headroom: tight enough that a stray import fails,
loose enough that a dependency patch does not. Raise a number only with a reason.
/dashboard 209 -> 215: the image field became an editable combobox on Radix Popover.
Replacing the preset chips was expected to pay for it and did not — ThemeToggle imports
ToggleGroup from radix-ui directly, so that dependency stays in the graph on every route
however many components stop using the wrapper. Popover is therefore purely additive
(~1.5 kB; its popper, portal, presence and dismissable-layer are already in via Select),
alongside the combobox's own keyboard and ARIA state machine and the project watcher.
Measured at 209.1 kB, set at actual + ~3% as above.
/_not-found 146 -> 167: the top bar moved into the root layout, so the landing page,
the dashboard, its loading state, its error boundary and the 404 stop each declaring
their own — which is what left the login page with a floating theme toggle and the 404
with no chrome, no <main> and no width at all. ThemeToggle is a client component, so
every route now carries Radix ToggleGroup and the shared Slot core (~20 kB gzip) that
only / and /dashboard used to. Measured 161.8 kB, up from 142.1. Deliberate: a 404
that cannot say which app it belongs to was the thing being fixed. /dashboard fell
209.1 -> 207.5 in the same change, because its header skeleton is now dead code.
/ 166 -> 171: restoring the headroom this number was supposed to have. It had been
seeded at 166.0 against a budget of 166 — flush, not 3% under — so the landing page
failed the gate on a change that did not touch it. The container list gained a filter
bar and paging; the landing page's own first-load moved 166.0 -> 166.2, entirely from
the shared layout graph re-splitting (12.9 + 3.6 kB became 9.0 + 7.7 kB), and its
route chunk is byte-identical. Set at actual + ~3% as the rule above intends.
/dashboard absorbed the feature itself at 211.7 -> 214.7, inside its existing budget:
the status chips reuse ToggleGroup, already in the graph via ThemeToggle, and the
origin checkboxes are native inputs rather than Radix Checkbox.
/dashboard 215 -> 222: the accessibility and shared-refresh work. Measured 215.0,
which is 0.0 kB over the previous number — the budget had been seeded flush against
214.7 rather than with the ~3% this file's own rule asks for, so it was one rounding
step from failing on a change that did not touch the route. Three additions account
for it: use-throttled-refresh, which container-row now calls instead of useRouter
directly; the ui/page column primitive, reached from the layout's header and footer;
and the skip link. All three are small — the whole delta is 0.3 kB — and the page
shell replaces seven hand-written className blobs, so the source is smaller than
before. Re-seeded at actual + ~3% as the rule above intends, rather than at actual.
/_not-found 167 -> 171: same measurement, 165.8 against 161.8 previously. The 404
renders the root layout, so it pays for the same shared graph the dashboard does —
the page primitive and the skip link — plus the layout re-splitting its chunks. It
was already the route with the least of its own code and the most inherited, which
is why a change to shared chrome shows up here most clearly.
/ 171 -> 179: the landing page became a freight yard with the sign-in card floating
in it — src/features/rail-yard, a canvas simulation of about 1,300 lines. Measured
166.2 -> 173.3, so the whole feature costs 7.1 kB gzip: the simulation, the routing
graph, the arc-length geometry, the renderer and the scene literal, with no new
dependency. Set at actual + ~3% as this file's rule intends.
Worth recording because it was the thing checked rather than assumed: /dashboard
moved 215.0 -> 215.2 and /_not-found 165.8 -> 165.6, both noise. The feature is
imported only from /'s page and RailYard is its own client boundary, so it lands in
that route's chunk and not in the shared layout graph — which is the failure mode a
client component on the landing page would otherwise have, and what the /_not-found
entry above is the worked example of. If those two numbers ever move for this
feature, that is a defect and not a budget question.
The log pane gained search with match highlighting, next/previous, a wrap toggle,
copy, download and an adaptive severity filter, and no number here moved for it. The
pane is next/dynamic and this script sums firstLoadChunkPaths, so its chunk is not
counted — which is the claim, and it was checked rather than assumed: none of the 14
first-load chunks on /dashboard contains log-pane-toolbar, log-view or any of the new
catalog keys. Measured /dashboard 216.0 and / 177.1, both inside budget; / is up on
its last recorded 173.3 for reasons this feature cannot reach, since nothing it
touches is imported from the landing page. What does land in the shared graph is one
empty div in log-pane-skeleton reserving the toolbar's height. No new dependency: the
highlight is <mark> over the accent tokens, the severity chips reuse the chip recipe
over the ToggleGroup already in every route via ThemeToggle, and the clipboard and
object URLs are platform APIs. If /dashboard ever moves for this feature, something
has leaked out of the dynamic chunk into container-row or log-pane-skeleton, and that
is a defect rather than a budget question.
Rejected: rendering the real toolbar inside LogPaneSkeleton so the two heights match
at every viewport rather than only where the control row fits on one line. It would
move the toolbar and its six lucide icons into the first load of every dashboard
visitor, most of whom never expand a row, to buy parity in a case only a narrow phone
reaches — and on a panel behind a click, which LHCI's CLS gate never mounts.
/dashboard 222 -> 229: the image existence check. Measured 222.2 against a budget of
222, which is 0.2 kB over — and the overage is the whole story rather than the cost.
That 222 was seeded at actual + ~3% when the route measured 215, and the accessibility,
container-action and idempotency work has since spent all of it, so this route was one
rounding step from failing on a change that did not touch it. Re-seeded at actual + ~3%
as this file's own rule intends.
What the feature actually costs the browser is use-image-check.ts and one Field prop,
and that was checked rather than assumed. IMAGE_PATTERN moved out of lib/validation.ts
into lib/registry/reference.ts specifically so the hook could hold the same regex
without importing zod — no chunk mentions zod, and neither parseImageReference nor the
Docker Hub alias table appears in any chunk either, so the parser and the allowlist are
tree-shaken and stay server-side. If zod or `index.docker.io` ever shows up in a
first-load chunk, something has imported lib/validation or the parser from a client
component, and that is a defect rather than a budget question.
/dashboard 229 -> 237: the deployment history behind the rollback control. Measured
229.6 against a budget of 229, so 0.6 kB over — which is the whole cost of the feature
in the browser: deployment-history.tsx, its fetch-on-expand, and three props on the
lifecycle dialog. No new dependency. Radix AlertDialog is already in the graph via the
row's own stop/restart/redeploy and destroy dialogs, so the confirmation is free, and
the list reuses StatusBadge, Text and relativeTime. Re-seeded at actual + ~3%.
Rejected, and this one is worth recording because it is counterintuitive: next/dynamic
with ssr:false around DeploymentHistory, the same treatment LogPane gets a few lines
above it in container-row.tsx. It works — the component genuinely leaves /dashboard's
first load, checked against route-bundle-stats.json rather than assumed — and the route
gets BIGGER: 229.6 -> 230.8. A second dynamic boundary plus the loading component the
panel needs to avoid a two-step reflow costs more than the 0.6 kB it defers. LogPane's
boundary earns itself because Radix ScrollArea sits behind it; there is nothing of that
size behind this one. Deferring a small component is not free, and this file is where
that number now lives.
Rejected: next/dynamic with ssr:false, which would keep / under the old number by
splitting the yard into a second request. The canvas is absolutely positioned and
contributes no layout, so it would cost nothing in stability — but it would make the
scene arrive a beat after the page, and a dynamic boundary is machinery this repo
has nowhere else. Paying the 7 kB honestly was preferred.
The dashboard became three routes: /dashboard (the container list), /dashboard/new (the
spin-up form) and /dashboard/billing (workspace spend and this app's usage totals).
Measured /dashboard 230.4, /dashboard/new 218.3, /dashboard/billing 208.0, and the two
new entries are seeded at actual + ~3% as this file's rule asks: /dashboard/new 225 and
/dashboard/billing 214. /dashboard stays at 237, because that number is already actual
+ ~3% for its new figure.
The prediction going in was that /dashboard would FALL, since it stops importing
SpinUpForm and with it the combobox, the Popover behind it, the key-value editor, the
disclosure, the preset catalog and use-image-check. It did not: 229.6 -> 230.4. The split
itself is real and was checked rather than assumed - grep for `idempotencyKey` across
static/chunks matches exactly one chunk, and route-bundle-stats.json lists it under
/dashboard/new only. What happened is that the cost moved rather than disappearing.
Summing the gzipped chunks each route does not share: the three have a common floor of
207.6 kB, on top of which /dashboard adds 22.8 for the list, /dashboard/new adds 10.7 for
the form and /dashboard/billing adds 0.4 for two cards. That floor is ~11.5 kB higher
than the shared graph was, because the tab strip is a client component in the DASHBOARD
LAYOUT: next-intl's client runtime and next/link's route machinery are now reached from
above the pages rather than from inside each route chunk, so what used to be route-local
is hoisted into a chunk all three pay for. /dashboard pays it either way, which is why
its own number barely moved.
So the win is not on /dashboard, and saying otherwise here would be wrong: it is that a
reader who only opens Billing now downloads 208 rather than 230, and that the two
lighter routes exist at all. If /dashboard ever grows past this by ~10 kB in one change,
check for `idempotencyKey` in its first-load chunks first - something importing
SpinUpForm transitively is a defect rather than a budget question.
Rejected: rendering the tab strip inside each page instead of the layout, which would
keep next-intl's client runtime out of the shared floor and hand ~11 kB back to
/dashboard/billing. It was refused on behaviour rather than bytes. A strip inside the
page sits BELOW the route's loading and error boundaries, so it is replaced by a
placeholder on every tab switch and absent entirely when a tab throws - which is the one
moment navigation matters most. e2e/skeleton.spec.ts asserts its bounding box is
unchanged across a switch, which is the check that would fail if this is ever revisited.
